evals.name: nextjs-turso-traffic
evals.prompt: i run a small next.js 15 app on vercel (app router, drizzle + turso, db client already wired in lib/db.ts). i want to know if chatgpt and claude are actually crawling my docs pages — google analytics shows me nothing at all which i'm guessing is because bots don't run js? can you set up server-side logging for AI crawlers and a basic admin page so i can actually look at it
evals.expected_output: Server-side capture (middleware) with a crawler catalogue and purpose taxonomy, an ai_visits table, fire-and-forget insert off the request path, prefetch skipping, IP verification plan, and an admin view that splits train/search/user rather than one blended AI-traffic number.
assertions: Classifies crawlers into a purpose taxonomy (train / search / user), rather than one blended 'AI bot' bucket
Treats OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User and GPTBot as three distinct agents with different purposes
Insert is fire-and-forget (waitUntil or unawaited promise) so tracking cannot block or fail the response
Skips Next.js router prefetch requests so real users aren't double-counted
Takes the client IP as the FIRST entry of x-forwarded-for, and stores it raw
Includes crawler verification against vendors' published IP ranges
verified is tri-state (NULL unchecked / 1 in-range / 0 failed-or-unprovable), not a plain boolean
Route matcher excludes static assets but still captures robots.txt / sitemap.xml
Explains that bots don't execute JavaScript, which is why client-side analytics shows nothing
Crawler regex order puts specific patterns before the generic ones they are substrings of
Admin dashboard is access-gated

evals.name: sveltekit-d1-both
evals.prompt: we have a sveltekit marketing site on cloudflare pages with a d1 database. leadership keeps asking 'are we showing up in AI search' and i want something in the repo that actually answers it — both which bots are hitting us and whether the models mention us versus our competitors. postgres isn't an option here and i'd rather not pay for profound or similar
evals.expected_output: Both halves adapted to SvelteKit hooks.server.ts + D1 (cf-connecting-ip / cf-ipcountry, ctx.waitUntil), SQLite DDL, three probe modes kept separate, share-of-voice denominator explained, and honest statement of what cannot be measured.
assertions: Capture is wired into SvelteKit's hooks.server.ts, not Next.js middleware
Uses Cloudflare's cf-connecting-ip / cf-ipcountry headers rather than Vercel's
DDL is SQLite/D1-compatible (no Postgres-only types such as jsonb or timestamptz)
Delivers both halves: crawler/referral traffic AND model-mention tracking
Keeps the three probe modes (memory / retrieval / index) as separate metrics
States that scores must never be averaged across probe modes
Share-of-voice denominator is answers naming anybody, not all answers
Includes a purpose taxonomy for crawlers (train / search / user)
States explicitly what this cannot measure (e.g. real-browser ChatGPT, or Google's AI reads)
Distinguishes a mention (model memory) from a citation (live retrieval)

evals.name: probe-scoring
evals.prompt: i already log AI bot hits into a table called ai_visits (kind/agent/path/ts). now i want the other half — a weekly job that asks a handful of prompts like 'best expense management tools for startups' across a few models and records whether we get named and who we lose to. i've got GEMINI_API_KEY and GROQ_API_KEY set up. how should i score this so the number isn't garbage?
evals.expected_output: Three probe modes distinguished (memory via Groq, retrieval via Gemini grounding, index needs a search key), share-of-voice denominator = answers naming anybody, mentioned/position/cited/competitors extraction, alias-matching lookaround caveat, temperature 0, per-probe pacing, dry mode, and never averaging across modes.
assertions: Distinguishes memory (no web access) from retrieval (grounded search) as separate modes
Maps Groq to the memory probe and Gemini grounding to the retrieval probe
Notes that an index/search-rank probe needs a search API key the user does not have
Answers the scoring question with denominator = answers naming anybody, excluding no-recommendation answers
Extracts all four signals: mentioned, position, cited, competitors
Uses temperature 0 for the memory probe
Paces requests per provider rather than globally, for free-tier rate limits
Provides a dry-run mode that spends nothing and writes nothing
States that averaging across modes is meaningless
Warns that brand-alias matching with \b breaks on names containing dots
Notes that competitors absent from the tracked list are invisible to share-of-voice
Keeps the full answer text so a score change can be explained
